extracted.intended_audience: scientists and technical readers (readers of Nature), including astronomers, meteorologists, engineers, and technical instrument-makers
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of technical and procedural guidance embedded in a scientific-news/current-topics page (e.g., apparatus approval conditions, observational procedures, and instrumentation requirements) for practitioners and informed readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for approval of receiving apparatus (broadcasting sets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving apparatus intended for use in connexion with the broadcasting services must fulfil conditions framed with the view of preventing the use, in such sets, of circuits which may 'regenerate' oscillations and thus cause disturbances at receiving stations within their re-radiation range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience indicated the need, for receiving apparatus handled by an unskilful user, for some form of control in the type and design of the apparatus; the specification accordingly should serve a useful purpose. Clause 10 (example provision) further provides that 'All sets sold under the broadcast licence shall bear the registered trade mark of the broadcasting company and the Post Office registered number.' Note: the BBC announcement applies to sets to be offered for sale by members of that corporation; it does not by itself represent Post Office policy. Recommendation: the Post Office should issue an official statement setting out its intended course in relation to grant of licences generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended headlight performance and beam-shaping criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions discussed for a satisfactory motor-car headlight include limits on illumination at a specified point ahead of the car and constraints on beam width and height to reconcile driver needs with glare to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: American conditions: at 100 feet ahead at a point 5 feet above the horizontal, the illumination must not exceed that due to a lamp of 750 candle power. Ministry of Transport (UK) conditions relate to width and height of the beam and place no restriction on intensity. Suggested compromise from Optical Society discussion: beam should have a candle power of 3000 in a direction half a degree below the horizontal and be reduced to 500–600 candle power in a direction one degree above the horizontal. As glare is due to contrast, it was further suggested that the car body and the road at the side of the car should be illuminated to some extent as well as the road in front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telescopic observational procedure for Mercury
rubrics_metrics.description: Telescopic observations of Mercury are required (since the exact time of the planet's rotation is doubtful), and certain practical observing methods improve the chance of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: observers without equatorial telescopes should pick up Mercury when visible to the naked eye and retain the disc in the field of view of their instrument until some time after sunrise, when it will have risen sufficiently above horizon vapours to permit a well-defined image. Mercury presents dusky markings which can be followed when weather is clear; the planet offers a better prospect for scrutiny than Venus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy for Perrine's periodic comet (example comet-search guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: When searching for a comet with uncertain perihelion date, use ephemerides computed for more than one assumed perihelion time and search in the region indicated by both solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Perrine's periodic comet should be looked for in the moon's absence; ephemerides were provided on two assumptions of the time of perihelion, and 'search should be made near the line joining the two positions for each date.' Practical note: present tables of R.A. and declination for the assumed times to guide searchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic parallax methods and error considerations for visual binary stars
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographic measures of parallaxes for several binary stars must take into account the irregularity of the combined image and orbital motion between exposures as potential sources of error; the method of using relative spectral-line shifts can yield absolute parallaxes for binaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigation should assess how image irregularity and change in relative positions due to orbital motion between exposures might introduce error; probable errors for photographic parallaxes seem comparable to single-star measures. For obtaining absolute parallaxes via relative shift of spectral lines due to different motion of components, it is necessary that both spectra be visible or that relative masses be known. The method has been applied to Alpha Centauri, Castor, and Sirius (bright star only); a list of candidate stars and the present/maximum differential motion is useful for planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and presentation choices for temperature-distribution charts (thermosynchrones/thermoisochrones)
rubrics_metrics.description: When producing charts of the distribution of temperature (thermosynchrones and thermoisocrones) across a region, reduction conventions and alternate presentations affect geographic utility and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hamberg's approach: base charts on many station observations (example: 232 Swedish and 83 Norwegian stations). Temperatures were reduced to sea-level for mean annual dates at which certain temperatures reign, though the author notes this reduces geographical usefulness for some purposes; therefore provide alternative chart pairs using actual (non-reduced) temperatures for spring and autumn (e.g., for 12°C and 0°C). Additionally produce a second series indicating average number of days with temperature above or below certain figures (termed thermoisocrones). Make clear which charts use reduced values and which use actual temperatures and include discussion of limitations.
